props.caption: Whoever holds the key reads everything

beats.vo: The obvious fix is to lock the column. Encrypt each password with a secret key.
Now the table shows scrambled text instead of mango at the rate one two three.
But encryption is built to be undone. Whoever holds the key can turn every row back into the original.
In twenty thirteen, Adobe was breached.
Its passwords were encrypted, not hashed, with a cipher called Triple D E S.

props.caption: One key for all of them · ~109M hints in plain text

beats.vo: Australia's privacy regulator later found that Adobe used a single encryption key for all of them.
About a hundred and nine million records also had a password hint, stored in plain text.
Adobe said about thirty-eight million active users were hit. The leaked file had about a hundred and fifty-three million records.

lines.text: A hint is a head start.
The site never needs to read it back.
It only needs to check it.

beats.vo: A hint like "my dog's name" gives a guesser a head start.
So encryption solved the wrong problem. The site never needed to read your password back. It only needs to check it.
The current guidelines reflect all of this.

props.quote: Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme.

beats.vo: The U S standards body Nist now requires salted password hashing in its guidelines, and recommends the highest cost a site can practically handle.

props.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT require subscribers to change passwords periodically.

beats.vo: Under these guidelines, sites must not force you to change your password on a schedule, like every ninety days. They must force a change if there's evidence it was compromised.

props.quote: a minimum of 15 characters in length

beats.vo: Sites must not demand symbols and mixed case. They ask for length instead. At least fifteen characters, if the password is your only login factor.

props.quote: SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords

beats.vo: And sites must check new passwords against a blocklist of commonly used, expected or compromised passwords.
